Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean and BDeRham.lean, and Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/ - perfectoid ring theory, but no perfectoid space
Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, sheaves on sites, and TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/ for the abelian-scheme side of the Siegel tower
TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/ and modular-curve level structures for the S5 modular-tower comparison
missing: perfectoid spaces themselves (tilting, almost mathematics, the almost purity theorem) - PerfectoidSpaces P7/P8 - plus PerfectoidQuotients Q4 and DiamondsAndVStacks D4/D6: diamonds, v-sheaves and their spatial theory; none of `perfectoid space`, `diamond`, `v-sheaf`, `tilt` occurs in the baseline

the whole Shimura stack: ShimuraData D4, ShimuraVarieties V6/V8 (canonical models at finite level, general data), ShimuraCompactifications C3/C5/C6 (toroidal and minimal compactifications) and PELModuli M2-M4 - `Shimura` has zero occurrences in the baseline
HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2-T6 (9 stages unique to this roadmap): canonical subgroups, the Hodge-Tate map for p-divisible groups, and the anticanonical locus with its radii
the anticanonical tower with Frobenius-approximation estimates and the perfectoidness of the completed direct limits, and the cusp/boundary construction on the minimal compactification (S1)
Scholze's Hodge-type descent through a symplectic embedding, and the Hansen-Johansson connected-tower descent to pre-abelian type with its finite-group quotients at infinite level (S2, S4)

AutomorphicBundles B1-B3 and the Boxer-Pilloni toroidal period-map theorem with the Levi-torsor pullback (S3, S6); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 and AdicEtaleGeometry A1 for the coefficient comparisons

PeriodsAndSpecialValues.targets: Comparison periods and determinant lines for motives; Deligne critical values and algebraicity; the formal-period algebra and the Nori torsor; regulator determinants and leading terms; integral fundamental lines with local corrections; equivariant Tamagawa-number statements; BSD and Bloch-Kato assembly; certified period/L-value computation; Picard-Fuchs equations and arithmetic mirror symmetry; multiple zeta values and mixed-Tate periods.
baselineHas: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean and DirichletContinuation.lean: completed zeta and Dirichlet L-functions with functional equations and Bernoulli special values - the PS.1 Dirichlet/Tate case's analytic half

TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/Regulator.lean: `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator` (line 91) and the Neron-Tate height pairing, plus `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.selmerGroup₂` (SelmerGroup.lean line 104) from 2-descent - the only regulator and Selmer objects present

Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Determinant.lean: `LinearMap.det` (line 179) with its base-change API, and Mathlib's `DerivedCategory` with t-structures - the raw shape of PS.4's determinant lines, though there is no determinant of a perfect complex and no Fitting-ideal API in the baseline
TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/ algebraic cycles and Mathlib's derived categories, the raw substrate for MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles
missing: motives with Betti/de Rham/etale realizations and comparison isomorphisms (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2/MC.4/MC.6) - `motive` and `MotivicCohomology` have zero occurrences in the baseline - hence period matrices and determinant lines are not even expressible (PS.0)
motivic L-functions from local Weil-Deligne data and the Deligne critical-value formalism, on top of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1/AL.4/AL.5 and AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 (PS.1)

the Nori period torsor and the formal-period algebra with its evaluation map (PS.2); Borel regulators R.7, elliptic regulators ER.5 and motivic/etale K-theory M.8 on a GeneralAlgebraicKTheory base that does not exist in the baseline (PS.3, PS.4)
NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.3 and the Burns-Flach/Fukaya-Kato equivariant Tamagawa formalism in relative K-groups with reduced norms (PS.5)

RankZeroOneBSD BSD.8 for the BSD adapters, which itself runs through EllipticCurveModularity R29.4, Heegner-point and Kato Euler systems, and AutomorphicCongruences back to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.6 (PS.6)

Polylogarithms P.1, the mixed-Tate category with the motivic fundamental group and coaction for multiple zeta values (PS.9), CrystallineCohomology CR.7 with Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs and Frobenius matrices (PS.8), and certified interval arithmetic for periods (PS.7)

676 upstream stages across 104 roadmaps with a longest chain of 107; its closure strictly contains AnalyticNumberTheory, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms, LefschetzPencils, EllipticCurveModularity, PELModuli, PadicFamilies and SerreWeight

judgements.reason: AdicSpaces is self-contained and half-built - Layers 0-2 are done in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/ - leaving the structure presheaf and stalks, Tate acyclicity, adic spaces with gluing and the Fargues-Fontaine curve with Kedlaya's interval rings. AnalyticNumberTheory has its own first two stages already in Mathlib's LSeries/riemannZeta, but the rest of the roadmap needs a zero-free region and PNT, explicit formulas and zero-density, Hecke and Artin L-functions, and then whole imported towers - Sato-Shintani prehomogeneous zeta over AdelicAlgebraicGroups and Igusa/motivic local zeta whose closure reaches GeneralAlgebraicKTheory, plus AutomorphicSpectralTheory's trace formula for Selberg zeta.

Both are single-subject TauCeti roadmaps with their bottom layers already built. AdicSpaces has four layers left (completed coordinate rings and stalks, Tate acyclicity, adic spaces and gluing, the FF curve with Kedlaya's strong-noetherian interval rings), while LieGroups has roughly seven spanning more distinct theories - Frobenius integrability, Lie's third theorem and the equivalence of categories, maximal tori and Weyl integration, complexification and real forms, Borel-Weil over flag manifolds (with essentially no holomorphic bundle theory in the baseline) and the Cartan/Iwasawa/KAK decompositions. AdicSpaces' remaining layers are individually heavier, which keeps the gap narrow.

ArithmeticDynamics needs several whole subjects that do not exist in the baseline: Berkovich analytic spaces with measures for DY.2 and DY.4 (`Berkovich` has zero occurrences), the Weil height machine for line bundles on general varieties, equidistribution for semipositive adelic metrized line bundles, and etale fundamental groups for arboreal representations - 34 upstream stages across 13 roadmaps on top of its own seven. LieGroups is one subject with Layers 0-1 and the Lie functor already built in TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/, leaving about seven layers of classical Lie theory and no external unbuilt roadmap.

Complex multiplication imports the general CM reciprocity theorem from ShimuraVarieties V5, which drags in Shimura data, canonical models, abelian schemes and the etale/Hodge comparison stack - 308 upstream stages across 50 roadmaps, longest chain 48 - and then still owes CM types and reflex norms, the uniformisation C/Lambda = E(C), class polynomials, every class field and algebraic Hecke characters. ArithmeticDynamics owes Berkovich spaces, the height machine for line bundles and an equidistribution theorem, but only 34 upstream stages with chain 14, and Mathlib's heights plus TauCeti's Neron-Tate package already cover DY.1's worked example.

Both start from almost nothing of their own, but the imports differ by an order of magnitude: HigherLocalFields needs Milnor K-theory and the norm-residue route through MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5d over a GeneralAlgebraicKTheory/StableHomotopyKTheory base (39 upstream stages, 8 roadmaps, chain 22), while ComplexMultiplication needs ShimuraVarieties V5's canonical models, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, ModularCurvesPartII, Neron models and automorphic Galois representations (308 upstream stages, 50 roadmaps, chain 48), on top of CM types, class polynomials and Hecke characters.

Their closures are disjoint, and HigherLocalFields' is larger and deeper (47 stages, chain 22, against 30 and chain 11). Metaplectic owes the Heisenberg group, Stone-von Neumann, the Weil index and theta kernels over an adelic/smooth-representation base much of which the baseline already supplies (Haar, additive-character Fourier transforms, SchwartzMap, Poisson summation, adele rings, Sp_2m, factor sets and projective representations). HigherLocalFields owes Milnor K-groups, higher duality with de Rham-Witt coefficients and Kato-Saito reciprocity on top of K2SymbolsBrauer and MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5d, i.e. a norm-residue and algebraic K-theory tower of which the baseline has literally nothing.

Metaplectic's substrate (Fourier analysis against additive characters, Schwartz spaces, Poisson summation, adeles, symplectic groups, central extensions by factor sets) is largely in the baseline, and its imports are 21 stages of adelic/smooth-representation theory. LefschetzPencils first needs the entire l-adic etale formalism it imports from EnhancedDerivedSheaves and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves - constructible sheaves, the six operations, duality and the perverse t-structure, none of which exists - before nearby and vanishing cycles, Picard-Lefschetz, pencil existence and the open-monodromy theorem: 111 upstream stages across 21 roadmaps, chain 34.

EllipticCurveModularity's upstream closure strictly contains all ten LefschetzPencils stages and adds 331 more: Galois representations and Tate modules, finite flat group schemes, Neron models, modular curves with their integral models and Jacobians, level and weight optimisation, Faltings' isogeny theorem and the full Khare-Wintenberger proof of Serre's conjecture. That is 444 upstream stages across 69 roadmaps with a longest chain of 89, against LefschetzPencils' 111 and 34.

EllipticCurveModularity has PELModuli inside its upstream closure (6 of its 7 stages) and then needs everything PEL does not touch: l-adic Galois representations, finite flat group schemes, Neron models, modular curves and their Jacobians, level and weight optimisation, Faltings finiteness and the whole strong Serre conjecture. PELModuli owes abelian schemes with polarisations and level structures, algebraic spaces with representability and deformation theory, and the Shimura comparison - large, but 69 upstream stages against 444.

PadicFamilies' closure contains PELModuli (5 of its 7 stages, via the Shimura/abelian-scheme route under the automorphic Galois representations it consumes) and adds a p-adic tower PELModuli never touches: Iwasawa algebras and measures, phi-Gamma modules and Iwasawa cohomology, Coleman power series, locally analytic distributions with Fredholm theory over affinoids, modular symbols, Selmer complexes and Kato's Euler system - 380 upstream stages against 69, on top of Hida families, eigenvarieties and control theorems of which the baseline has none.

The two closures overlap almost completely - 312 of SerreWeight's 329 stages lie inside PadicFamilies' - but PadicFamilies adds 76 stages SerreWeight never needs: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras, phi-Gamma modules and Iwasawa cohomology, Coleman power series, Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, locally analytic distributions with Fredholm theory, modular symbols, Selmer-Iwasawa cohomology, p-adic Hodge regulators and Kato's Euler system, and then its own Hida control theorems and eigencurve. SerreWeight adds only 17 stages (its own six plus parts of GL2 transfer, Neron models and modular curves) that PadicFamilies lacks.

SerreWeight's closure already contains 166 of PerfectoidShimura's 198 stages - including the diamond and perfectoid layers it reaches through ModularCurvesPartII and WeightsInEtaleCohomology - and then adds 163 more: 20 stages of ModularCurvesPartII, 12 of GL2 transfer, Deligne weights and purity, classical adic etale cohomology, smooth representations of local groups, endoscopic transfer, Neron models, Hilbert modular and Shimura curves, and algebraic modular forms with Serre weights. PerfectoidShimura's 32 unique stages (canonical subgroups and Hodge-Tate maps, automorphic bundles, the top of PerfectoidSpaces, its own eight) are real but far smaller; 329 stages and chain 54 against 198 and chain 41.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues has 676 upstream stages across 104 roadmaps with a longest chain of 107, and its closure strictly contains EllipticCurveModularity, PadicFamilies, SerreWeight, PELModuli, LefschetzPencils, Metaplectic and AnalyticNumberTheory; it must build motives with realizations, algebraic K-theory and regulators, the Nori period torsor, equivariant Tamagawa formalism and the mixed-Tate motivic fundamental group, of which the baseline has nothing. PerfectoidShimura's 190 upstream stages - perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Shimura varieties with compactifications, canonical subgroups - are a large but strictly smaller stack.

LieGroups is one subject whose bottom is built: TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/ already has lieExp, Ad, ad = d(Ad) and the Lie functor, leaving roughly seven layers of classical Lie theory and no external unbuilt roadmap. AnalyticNumberTheory likewise has its first two stages in Mathlib, but still owes a zero-free region and the prime number theorem, explicit formulas and zero-density, Hecke and Artin L-functions, Halasz-type mean values, and then two imported towers: Sato-Shintani prehomogeneous zeta over AdelicAlgebraicGroups with Igusa/motivic local zeta reaching GeneralAlgebraicKTheory, and AutomorphicSpectralTheory's spectral decomposition and trace formula for Selberg zeta, plus C*-algebraic KMS theory for Bost-Connes - 63 upstream stages across 18 roadmaps.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues has all seven PELModuli stages inside its upstream closure and adds motives with Betti/de Rham/etale realizations, algebraic and motivic K-theory with Borel and elliptic regulators, the Nori period torsor, integral fundamental lines, equivariant Tamagawa numbers, the rank-zero/one BSD route (which itself runs back through EllipticCurveModularity) and mixed-Tate periods: 676 upstream stages against PELModuli's 69.

They share 69 stages of etale/adic groundwork, but PerfectoidShimura needs 129 more that LefschetzPencils does not - ShimuraVarieties with canonical models, ShimuraData, ShimuraCompactifications, PELModuli, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups, PerfectoidSpaces and PerfectoidQuotients, AInfCohomology, PadicHodgeTheory and RelativeFarguesFontaine - while LefschetzPencils needs only 52 that PerfectoidShimura does not (DeligneWeightsAndPurity, DiamondEtaleCohomology, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology and its own ten stages). 190 upstream stages with chain 41 against 111 with chain 34.

AdicSpaces builds on nothing but Mathlib topological algebra and already has Layers 0-2 done in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/, leaving stalks and sheafiness, adic spaces with gluing, and the Fargues-Fontaine curve. ComplexMultiplication cannot even state CM.2 without ShimuraVarieties V5's canonical models and CM reciprocity, and behind that abelian schemes, Shimura data, modular curves, Neron models and automorphic Galois representations - 308 upstream stages across 50 roadmaps with a longest chain of 48, with `Shimura`, `CM type` and `class polynomial` all absent from the baseline.

Metaplectic owes nine stages of Heisenberg/Weil-representation theory over 21 upstream stages of adelic and smooth-representation theory, with much of its analytic substrate (Haar, additive-character Fourier transforms, Schwartz spaces, Poisson summation, adeles, Sp_2m, central extensions) already in the baseline. SerreWeight owes 323 upstream stages across 50 roadmaps with chain 54: residual Galois representations, integral models of modular curves with their bad fibres and character groups, Neron models, finite flat group schemes, Jacquet-Langlands transfer and quaternionic Shimura curves, and beneath them - via ModularCurvesPartII R13.6 and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.3 - the whole l-adic etale and weights machinery.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues has all eight PadicFamilies stages inside its upstream closure (through RankZeroOneBSD and the automorphic p-adic L-function route) and then adds motives with realizations and comparison periods, algebraic and motivic K-theory with Borel and elliptic regulators, the Nori period torsor, integral fundamental lines and equivariant Tamagawa numbers, Picard-Fuchs/crystalline comparisons and the mixed-Tate motivic fundamental group: 676 upstream stages across 104 roadmaps against PadicFamilies' 380 across 66.

AnalyticNumberTheory's headline stages are the closer of the two - Mathlib already has LSeries, riemannZeta with its functional equation, Dirichlet L-functions and Dirichlet's theorem, and Tau Ceti has Perron inversion and Chebotarev - but the roadmap as a whole owes far more: PNT and zero-free regions, explicit formulas and zero-density, Hecke and Artin L-functions, Halasz-type mean values, and then AN.8's Sato-Shintani prehomogeneous zeta with Igusa/motivic local integrals (whose closure runs to GeneralAlgebraicKTheory) and AN.9's Selberg/spectral zeta over AutomorphicSpectralTheory plus C*-algebraic KMS theory for Bost-Connes: 63 upstream stages against ArithmeticDynamics' 34. ArithmeticDynamics owes Berkovich analytic spaces and measures, the height machine for line bundles, the small-point equidistribution theorem and etale fundamental groups for arboreal representations, which is why the margin is not wide.

HigherLocalFields owes n-local fields, Milnor K-theory with residues and norms, higher duality and Kato-Saito reciprocity over a K2SymbolsBrauer and MotivicEtaleKTheory base - 39 upstream stages across 8 roadmaps, chain 22. EllipticCurveModularity owes 444 upstream stages across 69 roadmaps with chain 89: Galois representations and Tate modules, finite flat group schemes, Neron models, modular curves with integral models and Jacobians, Faltings' isogeny theorem, level and weight optimisation, and the full Khare-Wintenberger proof of Serre's conjecture, none of which exists in the baseline.

They share only 30 stages. LefschetzPencils needs 91 more - EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology, DiamondEtaleCohomology and DiamondSixOperations, DeligneWeightsAndPurity, AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons and its own ten stages of nearby/vanishing cycles, Picard-Lefschetz, pencil existence and open monodromy - against PELModuli's 46 (ShimuraVarieties, ShimuraData, abelian schemes, complex comparison, its own seven). 111 upstream stages with chain 34 against 69 with chain 20, and the etale six-operations formalism underneath LPV is entirely absent from the baseline.

Metaplectic's 30-stage closure (chain 11) is built on Fourier analysis, Schwartz spaces, Haar measure, adeles and symplectic groups that the baseline largely supplies; what it owes is the Heisenberg/Weil-representation theory itself plus smooth representations and automorphic forms on reductive groups. PerfectoidShimura's 198-stage closure (chain 41) needs perfectoid spaces and almost purity, diamonds and v-stacks, Shimura data with canonical models and compactifications, PEL moduli, canonical subgroups and Hodge-Tate period maps - and the baseline has no perfectoid space, no diamond and no Shimura variety at all.

LieGroups is self-contained, with lieExp, Ad, ad = d(Ad) and the Lie functor already in TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/, leaving about seven layers of classical Lie theory and no unbuilt external roadmap. ComplexMultiplication has no layer built and imports the general CM reciprocity theorem from ShimuraVarieties V5, hence Shimura data, canonical models, abelian schemes with polarisations, modular curves, Neron models and automorphic Galois representations - 308 upstream stages across 50 roadmaps, chain 48 - before it can even begin its own CM types, class polynomials, ring class fields and Hecke characters.
